# S51 — Supersede part of a record (narrow its scope) instead of all of it

**Findings:** ork adj 168 ui.structured-questions, 2026-10-25 · **Size:** M · **Tree:**

**Not in this slice:**

## Why

ork's adj 168 (ui.structured-questions) changes two decided records, #104 (no structured answer options) and #109 (Enter submits, no confirm), only for structured questions; free-text answers keep #104 and #109. `adj supersede OLD --by NEW` replaces the whole record: OLD becomes superseded (internal/model/transition.go:75) and leaves `adj context`, which would drop the free-text rule. Today the only way is a full supersede plus restating the kept parts in NEW. ork's adj 169 (ui.sidebar-running against #82) has the same shape.

## Failing tests

Red first, table-driven; `t.TempDir()` under `.cache/tmp` with an explicit `cli.Env.Root`.
- `adj narrow OLD --by NEW --scope TEXT` on two decided records leaves OLD `decided`, adds the link to OLD (NEW's ID and the scope) and to NEW (OLD's ID), appends one `narrow` history entry to each (notes `by NEW: SCOPE` and `narrows OLD`), and prints OLD's ID. OLD stays in `adj context` with a line naming NEW and the scope; NEW's line names OLD.
- `adj show OLD`, `adj show NEW` and `--json` print the link both ways. `adj context --format json` carries it as optional keys.
- A record may be narrowed by several records. Narrowing the same pair twice is a no-op or exit 1 (C32); it never adds a second link.
- Exit 2: a missing or non-positive ID, no `--by`, no or blank `--scope`, a scope on several lines, OLD equal to NEW, an extra argument. Exit 1, nothing written: an unknown ID, or either record not `decided` (OLD's status is checked before NEW's, and the message names the status).
- If NEW cannot be written, OLD is put back, as for supersede (C136).
- `adj lint`: a narrow link to a record that is not `decided`, or to an ID with no file, is an error; a link listed on only one side is an error; a record whose narrowing record was later superseded is a warning (C32).
- `adj supersede` and its tests are unchanged; a full supersede of a narrowed record still works.
- `adj renumber` lists a narrow link to a colliding ID as it does supersede links.
- The agent snippet names narrow among the never-run commands and stays within 1800 bytes (`ai_test.go`).
- Mutation-check: removing the scope from the context line, and removing the restore of OLD, each fail a test.

## Implement

Owner decision (2026-11-02): a new owner-only command `adj narrow OLD --by NEW --scope TEXT [--root DIR]`; `adj supersede` is unchanged.

Proposed under C32 for the implementer to record with `slicer catalog add --kind decision` (the reviewer checks, the owner may overrule), keeping the record format forward compatible (S46):
- Record fields, both omitted when empty: on OLD `narrowed_by`, a list of `{"id": N, "scope": "TEXT"}`; on NEW `narrows`, a list of IDs. A new history event `narrow` on both records.
- `show` prints `Narrowed by: NEW (SCOPE)` and `Narrows: OLD`. `context` md appends the scope to the decision line; the JSON gains optional `narrowed_by` and `narrows` keys.
- Lint check names: `narrow-state` (a link to a record that is not decided), `dangling-link` (existing check, extended), `narrow-asymmetric`.
- Order of writes: OLD first, then NEW, with the restore of OLD on failure, as `adj supersede` does.
1. Record the C32 choices. 2. Red tests, then model, commands, render, lint. 3. Docs and the agent snippet.
